topic: Care plan documentation in mental health

audits.title: An audit of Individual Care Plan (ICP) in Dublin North City and County (DNCC) child and adolescent mental health service (CAMHS)
audits.standard: Established service policy on individual care plans (ICP): every patient should have a care plan with key worker, formulation, goals, action plan, copy to young person/parents, review date and projected discharge date
audits.setting: Dublin North City and County child and adolescent mental health service (CAMHS) team
audits.intervention: Findings and intervention discussed at the multidisciplinary team meeting and wider DNCC CAMHS academic meeting; intervention not otherwise described
audits.other_findings: Re-audit every three months was recommended, to be carried out by multidisciplinary team members.
audits.citation: Egbuta U, Howley C, Selvarajoo A, Iqbal M, Meskauskait D. An audit of Individual Care Plan (ICP) in Dublin North City and County (DNCC) child and adolescent mental health service (CAMHS). BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S77-S78.

audits.title: Audit Report on Leave and Observation Documentation in Admission Plans for Out-of-Hours Admissions
audits.standard: Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003 and local risk protocols: MHA status, leave and observation levels documented

cycle1.result: Observation levels documented 15.4%; leave status documented 1.9% (13.5% failed to mention leave at all); MHA status 82.7%

audits.intervention: Posters in resident doctor work areas prompting legal status and safety monitoring plans

cycle2.result: Observation levels 55.2%; leave status 65.5%; MHA status 75.9%

audits.other_findings: MHA status documentation stayed roughly the same.
audits.citation: Hokkanen T, Ahmad R, Alhadi R. Audit Report on Leave and Observation Documentation in Admission Plans for Out-of-Hours Admissions. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S270-S271. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11573.

audits.title: Enhancing Medical Governance of Care Within an EIP Service
audits.standard: Service standard operational policy: medical CPA review every 6 months
audits.setting: Brighton Early Intervention in Psychosis service, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
audits.other_findings: Overdue reviews were linked with clinical stability, long caseload time and change of lead practitioner; an alert spreadsheet and policy sessions were set up before planned re-audit.
audits.citation: Veldmeijer C, Perera S, Fuller M, Kavanagh G, Whale R. Enhancing Medical Governance of Care Within an EIP Service. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S144-S144.

audits.title: File audit to assess sustained fidelity to a recovery and wellbeing oriented mental health service model: an Australian case study.
audits.standard: Collaborative Recovery Model fidelity, assessed with the 17-item GAP-IQ audit tool

cycle1.result: Baseline file audit of consumer support plans (figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Training and coaching practices implemented by the organisation (not formally evaluated as the cause).

cycle2.result: Significant increase in fidelity to CRM practices, with 16 of 17 GAP-IQ items significantly improved.

audits.other_findings: The 'Action Plan Review' item did not improve.
audits.citation: Jones CL, Deane FP, Wolstencroft K, Zimmermann A. File audit to assess sustained fidelity to a recovery and wellbeing oriented mental health service model: an Australian case study. Arch Public Health. 2019;77:50. doi:10.1186/s13690-019-0377-6. PMID: 31768253.

audits.title: Improving the efficiency and person-centredness of occupational therapy input into care-plans in a forensic mental health and rehabilitation service.
audits.standard: Goal Directed Care Plan audit tool; aim of 82% person-centredness of OT input into care plans by December 2023
audits.setting: Occupational therapy in forensic and rehabilitation mental health services, Derbyshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Person-centredness of care plans 63.64% in rehabilitation service and 65.15% in forensic service.

audits.intervention: QI project using patient feedback, more efficient admission process, staff training with an example person-centred care plan input, and monthly audit by band 6 and 7 OTs reported to assurance meetings.

cycle2.result: Person-centredness 84.34% in rehabilitation service and 95.45% in forensic service.

audits.other_findings: Improved admission efficiency released time for care planning; sustainability built in through monthly audit reporting.
audits.citation: Ige JJI, Alston A, Boreland V, Caudwell M, Ashbourne R, Ford B, et al.. Improving the efficiency and person-centredness of occupational therapy input into care-plans in a forensic mental health and rehabilitation service. BMJ Open Qual. 2024;13(4):e002883. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2024-002883. PMID: 39448088.

audits.title: An Audit of Mental Health Care Plans in Community Mental Health Services for Older Persons in Rural Communities in a State in Australia.
audits.standard: Quality standards for care plan documentation
audits.setting: Rural community mental health teams for older persons

cycle1.result: 72.1% had a care plan; cognition documented 32%, self-harm risk 29.8%, visual impairment 5.5%, hearing 5%, Advance Care Directives 35.4%.

audits.other_findings: Authors recommend a care plan template specific to rural older patients.
audits.citation: Lecamwasam D, Gupta N, Battersby M. An Audit of Mental Health Care Plans in Community Mental Health Services for Older Persons in Rural Communities in a State in Australia. J Behav Health Serv Res. 2022;49(2):162-189. doi:10.1007/s11414-021-09775-z. PMID: 35000103.
